Sentence (English): I'm a family of four with two kids.
Comments (English): I'm a family of four with two kids. Since both parents work, the kids eat at home, and the only food we have is snacks, my husband's lunch box, and a water bottle on weekends or weekdays, but even that was stressful, so I bought a dishwasher. I was debating a lot between a 6-person and a 12-person one, but when I used a 6-person one before, nothing could fit. Since I take out a lot of things when cooking, I decided to buy a 12-person one, but since it's a lease, a built-in one won't work, and I wondered if a freestanding one would work here, but I just ordered it and waited for the technician to contact me. I took a picture of the place I wanted it installed, and if the length of the hose is long, an additional fee of 20,000-30,000 won will be charged. / Drilling fee? I heard that it costs 10,000 won and visited the next day. They said that I didn't need to add the length, so I only paid 10,000 won for the installation fee. I saw a review that said the screws were rusty after a month, so I checked before installation, but there was no removal. It's easy to operate because you just have to press the power button, and it's good that there's a 2/1 setting when you write the amount. When I tried it twice, the one I did washed well, but when my husband played Tetris, there were a few things that didn't work. It seems that kimchi stains and larvae need to be removed. Still, the quality of life has definitely increased, and I'm very satisfied with the 12-person use. It would have been the same if it had been for 6 people. The part where the mop holder was cut was reattached with strong bond when I moved. I used the all-in-one detergent and I like it~~ (Re-review) I'm using it well! It's okay to wash, and if you put something oily in it, it washes well. However, the moisture doesn't dry well even if you leave it for a day. It seems better for your mental health to just wipe it with a dishcloth and organize it. - I recommend Comet's ultra-fine dishcloth. It dries moisture well.

Sentence (English): I'm a family of four with two kids.
Comments (English): I'm a family of four with two kids. Since both of us work, the kids eat at home. Food is limited to snacks on weekends or weekdays, lunch boxes for my husband, and water bottles. Even that was stressful, so I bought a dishwasher. I debated between a 6-seater and a 12-seater, but when I tried the 6-seater before, it didn't fit anything. It's a stainless steel dishwasher that takes out a lot of things while cooking. I decided to buy the 12-seater, but since it's a lease, a built-in one wouldn't work. I was also unsure if a freestanding dishwasher would work in this location. So I just ordered it and waited for the installer to contact me. I sent him pictures of the installation location I wanted. If the hose is too long, an additional 20,000-30,000 won will be charged. (There's a 10,000 won drilling fee.) After hearing the explanation, the installer came the next day. He said the length wouldn't need to be increased, so I only paid the 10,000 won installation fee. I saw a review where someone said the screws had rusted a month later. I checked before installation, but they hadn't removed any. It's easy to operate, just press the power button. It also has a 2/1 setting for small quantities, which is nice. When I tried it twice, it cleaned everything I did well. When my husband played Tetris, there were a few things that didn't work. It seems like it needs to be cleaned up after kimchi stains and larvae. Still, my quality of life has definitely improved, and I'm very satisfied with the 12-person option. It would have been just as good if it had been for 6 people. The cut part of the mop holder was reattached with strong adhesive when I moved out. I used Gomgom All-in-One, and it's great. (Review) I'm using it well! It washes well, and it washes well even when I put in oily items. However, it doesn't dry well even after a day. It's better for my mental health to just wipe it down with a dishcloth. I recommend the Comet microfiber dishcloth. It dries well.

Sentence (English): Honest Review: Bosch 100 Series Dishwasher for a Family Home.
Comments (English): [ Great dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || Honest Review: Bosch 100 Series Dishwasher for a Family Home. After months of dealing with a noisy, unreliable dishwasher, we finally upgraded to the Bosch 100 Series Dishwasher, and overall, it's been a great addition to our busy household. With three kids, constant meals, and never-ending dishes, we needed something reliable, spacious, and (most importantly) quiet. Here's my take on it after using it for a while. What We Love:. ✅ Super Quiet – With little kids running around, nap time is sacred in our house. Thankfully, this dishwasher is whisper-quiet compared to our old one. At around 48-50 dBA, you can barely hear it unless you're standing right next to it. I can actually run it after dinner without worrying about waking anyone up. ✅ Gets the Job Done – Even after spaghetti nights and sticky peanut butter sandwiches, our dishes come out sparkling clean. Bosch's PrecisionWash™ technology really does a good job of adjusting to how dirty the dishes are, so I don't have to pre-rinse everything (which saves time and water). ✅ Spacious & Family-Friendly Layout – I love how much I can fit in here! The adjustable upper rack is a game-changer when I need to fit taller water bottles or big mixing bowls. The silverware basket is also well-designed, so even my kids' small utensils get cleaned properly. ✅ Energy & Water Efficient – Since we run our dishwasher daily (sometimes twice a day), it was important for us to have something ENERGY STAR® certified. I've already noticed a slight drop in our water usage, which is a nice bonus! A Few Downsides:. ❌ Drying Could Be Better – This model doesn't have a heating element, so plastics tend to stay wet unless I crack the door open after the cycle. Not a dealbreaker, but something to keep in mind if you hate towel-drying. ❌ Takes a While to Finish – The regular cycle is pretty long (2+ hours), which isn't ideal when I need dishes quickly. Luckily, there's a Speed60 setting that helps when I'm in a rush. Final Thoughts:. If you're looking for a reliable, quiet, and spacious dishwasher that can handle the daily chaos of a family home, the Bosch 100 Series is a solid pick. It may not have all the fancy features of higher-end models, but it cleans well, saves energy, and is quiet enough to run anytime. As long as you don't mind cracking the door open for better drying, it's a great family-friendly option! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (4/5 stars). Would I buy it again? Yes! It's been a lifesaver in our kitchen.

So I'm looking forward to more service appointments in the future, but hope to have better service via Best Buy and Geek Squad as they've been great in the past. Just sucks that it feels like any appliance is a gamble anymore, nothing holds up.

Connecting the water was easy, and the instructions were intuitive, so installation was no problem. User Reviews & Performance Evaluation: Cleaning Power: Grease removal passed! Automatic Door Opening: After washing, the door automatically opens to quickly release moisture from the inside. This is convenient because there's no need to open the door, and it seems to improve drying performance. Noise: It's quieter than expected! I didn't even notice it running at night. Water Usage: It's definitely more water-efficient than washing dishes by hand. It uses about 6 liters per wash, which is very economical. Storage Space: Although it's said to be suitable for 6 people, it's difficult to fit large pots and pans. You'll need to arrange the dishes carefully to maximize storage. It's sufficient for a household of 2-3 people, but it might not be enough for a large family. Water Usage: It's definitely more water-efficient than washing dishes by hand. It uses about 6 liters per wash, which is very economical. Reason for Purchase & Expectations: My joints are weak, so washing greasy dishes would strain my fingers and force me to visit a Korean medicine doctor. So, after much deliberation, we decided to purchase a dishwasher. We're a two-person household, and we had very strict selection criteria. An auto-opening feature was a must (prevents water stains and odors). A clean design (harmonizes with the kitchen). Excellent cleaning power (cleans grease stains). Ease of use (no complicated operations requiring multiple buttons!). Convenient water supply (easy installation). After comparing products from several manufacturers and debating for several days, we finally chose this one! Unboxing & First Impressions: The white color blends well with our kitchen interior. A clean, uncluttered design! It's more compact than I expected, easily fitting next to a small sink. The interior is well-organized, and I liked the sturdy stainless steel basket. Connecting the water was easy, and the instructions were intuitive, so installation was no problem. User Reviews & Performance Evaluation: Cleaning Power: Grease removal passed! Even after grilling pork belly, it cleaned the dishes thoroughly. I was satisfied with the cups, bowls, and cutlery coming out clean and stain-free. Automatic Door Opening: After washing, the door automatically opens to quickly release moisture from the inside. This is convenient because there's no need to open the door, and it seems to improve drying performance. Noise: It's quieter than expected! I didn't even notice it running at night. Water Usage: It's definitely more water-efficient than washing dishes by hand. It uses about 6 liters per wash, which is very economical. Storage Space: Although it's said to be suitable for 6 people, it's difficult to fit large pots and pans. You'll need to arrange the dishes carefully to maximize storage. It's sufficient for a household of 2-3 people, but it might not be enough for a large family. People like this, consider this! Large families of 4 or more people may find the capacity insufficient. People who frequently use large pots and frying pans (you may need to wash them separately). Sentence (English): A genuine review from a 26-year-old couple!
Comments (English): [ Recommended for 2-3 person households; consider carefully for 4 or more people! ] || ---------------- || A genuine review from a 26-year-old couple! A dishwasher, considered a must-have for newlyweds, has finally arrived in our home! This is the Midea Automatic Door Opening Dishwasher (6-Place, MDWMT0601W-A-KR, White). Reason for Purchase & Expectations: My joints are weak, so washing greasy dishes would strain my finger muscles, forcing me to visit an acupuncture clinic. After much deliberation, I decided to get a dishwasher. As a two-person household, we established strict selection criteria. Automatic door opening was a must (to prevent limescale odors). The design had to be clean (to harmonize with the kitchen). It had to have good cleaning power (clean even grease). It had to be easy to use (no complicated operations requiring multiple button presses!). Water supply had to be convenient (easy to install). After comparing products from various manufacturers and deliberating for several days, we finally chose this product! Unboxing & First Impressions: The white color blended well with the kitchen interior. A clean, minimalist design! The size was more compact than I expected, so it fit perfectly even next to a small sink. The interior was well-organized, and I liked the sturdy stainless steel basket. Connecting the water supply wasn't difficult, and the instructions were intuitive, so I had no trouble installing it. User Review & Performance Evaluation. Washing Power. Grease removal gets a passing grade! Even greasy dishes after grilling pork belly are cleaned perfectly. Cups, bowls, and cutlery are all wiped clean and come out stain-free, which I was satisfied with. Automatic Door Opening Function. The door opens automatically when the wash is finished, allowing internal moisture to escape quickly. It is convenient because you don't need to open the door manually, and it feels like the drying performance is even better! Noise. It is quieter than expected! It isn't bothersome even when running at night. Water Consumption. It definitely saves water compared to hand washing. It uses about 6 liters per wash, which is very economical. Storage Space. Although it is rated for 6 people, it is difficult to fit large pots or frying pans. You have to arrange the dishes carefully to fit as much as possible! It is sufficient for a household of 2-3 people, but it might be insufficient for a large family. Summary of Pros & Cons. Pros. Improved drying performance thanks to the automatic door opening function. Its compact size makes it suitable for studio apartments and newlywed homes. It is quiet, so you can use it comfortably even at night. It features an audible alert to notify you after the dishwashing cycle is complete. It is economical due to its water-saving effects. Its excellent cleaning power ensures that removing grease is no problem. It is easy to install and convenient with automatic water supply. Cons: It is difficult to fit large pots or frying pans. The capacity is somewhat small for families of 4 or more. Additional work may be required to neatly organize the water connection hose. Recommended for & Not Recommended for: We recommend this to! Newlyweds, 1-2 person households. Those living in studio apartments or with small kitchens. Those who want to reduce hand washing but have limited space. Those who find washing dishes after late-night snacks a hassle (like us). Those with weak joints or wrist pain (it significantly reduces the burden of dishwashing!). Those who should consider this: The capacity may be insufficient for large families of 4 or more. Those who frequently use large pots and frying pans (they may need to be washed separately). Overall & Final Rating: 4.7 / 5.0 points! "A dishwasher tailored for newlyweds and 1-2 person households that fits well even in small spaces! The automatic door opening feature is convenient, and the cleaning power is satisfactory. However, there might be insufficient space to fit large cooking utensils." 3-Line Summary! I then shared my findings and video of the leak with Samsung to try to get them to come out and fix it again but they kept saying that it was an installation issue so they can only fix it outside of warranty and would cost us an arm and a leg (more than it would to simply buy a new unit! ). I am done with Samsung and will never buy one of their stuff again. Buyer beware! Not only do their products break, but their customer service is also horrible.

I believe it's because it's a European dishwasher and there's restrictions on power consumption so it doesn't have a heating ring in the bottom to help dry the dishes. A new version actually pops the door open partially after the cycle is over. And the next level version which I believe the Bosch 800 has some crystal drying mechanism. The reason I bought the Bosch is it has a strong track record of lasting a long time. My previous dishwasher was a GE higher and model and it still died relatively early. The Bosch dishwashers are a little bit more expensive than comparable models. I think I paid like two or $300 extra above other models. But in the long run, I think we'll have more value.

Sentence (English): So far, it's a great dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Great Dishwasher, though it lacks features ] || ---------------- || So far, it's a great dishwasher. I have my likes and dislikes of course. This replaced a GE dishwasher that had some good features we would have loved to have had again. One of which, the first one is one my wife liked and was looking for, bottle sprayers, where the nozzle goes up into the bottle. The other feature was the digital display that showed how long the wash time would be per the wash settings you selected. Finally, there wasn't a "top rack" or "bottom rack" when it came where to put dishes. A very convenient feature. However, that dishwasher had reliability issues that the reviews we read of the KitchenAid 360 Max Jets didn't seem to have. The door seems much more substantial, and the build quality seems better as well. My wife loves the third rack. The second, adjustable rack, at first seemed to possibly be useful, but we never have a situation where it helps. That's because when it is all the way up, there is more room for taller items on the bottom. When adjusted down, it almost, if not entirely, splits the difference so there is no room for taller items. Sentence (English): Bought almost a year ago.
Comments (English): Bought almost a year ago. Extremely disappointed with this dishwasher. My friend has an older 300 series that is quieter and dries better than our new Benchmark series. First dishwasher we received made loud grinding noises and smelled like hot tar when it ran. The replacement dishwasher is better as it doesn't smell like hot tar. The door is flimsy with plastic parts that feel like it might break any time we open or close it. Did not expect this from Bosch, especially on their benchmark series. Ours is much louder than 38 decibels. Our living room and kitchen are open concept so the low decibels was a must on our list. But, it's loud enough that we need to turn up the TV in the living room when it's running. It doesn't dry, even with CrystalDry and sanitize options selected. Water pools and drips from the edges on the third rack. Have to leave door open for more than a day to get the walls to dry. Silverware in the 3rd rack does not get clean and the rack is too shallow for any of our other items. Advise testing in warehouse if possible before purchase to check the rack configurations/sizes. We were expecting a top performing machine and feel like we wasted money on this item. The first and second racks wash dishes very well.

Ours is much louder than 38 decibels. Our living room and kitchen are open concept so the low decibels was a must on our list. But, it's loud enough that we need to turn up the TV in the living room when it's running. It doesn't dry, even with CrystalDry and sanitize options selected. Water pools and drips from the edges on the third rack. Have to leave door open for more than a day to get the walls to dry. Silverware in the 3rd rack does not get clean and the rack is too shallow for any of our other items. Advise testing in warehouse if possible before purchase to check the rack configurations/sizes. We were expecting a top performing machine and feel like we wasted money on this item.  The first and second racks wash dishes very well.

At the very least, clearer guidelines and oversight should be in place to prevent installers from unnecessarily inflating costs.Thank you for considering this feedback. I hope Costco will take steps to address this issue and ensure a better experience for all customers moving forward.

I'm currently using an oven, but I rarely use it, and since it was already installed in my apartment, I was thinking of taking it out and putting a dishwasher in its place. I was looking at 3 brands to see which one would be good, and the beige color was definitely the lightest and best suited to my house, and I wanted LG more than Samsung. I used a small dishwasher for 6 people before. First of all, when I looked into the dishwasher, there wasn't much difference, and the performance seemed to be almost the same. I thought detergent was important, and I wanted to buy a big one if possible, so I decided to get a 14-person one. These days, the products that are coming out have a knife holder, so I was very satisfied. When choosing other items, I was worried about whether or not to include the option to put in and remove the frying pan, but when I went to the store, I found that it was installed so that it was quite small. I usually use a large frying pan, about 28 cm, and it is best to wash it upside down so that the water touches it. Depending on the option, the price difference was about 100,000-200,000 won. I thought it would be okay to have it, but I didn't think I would use it much even if I spent more money, so I bought it without it. Honestly, I don't think the cleaning power is that good, and even a 14-person one can eat rice and soup bowls for about 5 people, and if you take out the pot and frying pan, you think it's small. Since it's cheap, if you're going to buy it, buy a big one. Prices vary widely from site to site, so I think the best way is to buy it at a cheaper price at the right time.

Any value assumed from the sale price has been erased by having to hire someone to do the installation and take another day off of work to be home while work is done. No review of the dishwasher as it currently is sitting in the foyer waiting for work I thought was paid for.

Sentence (English): This is our second Bosch dishwasher.
Comments (English): This is our second Bosch dishwasher. It's VERY quiet and the quality is very, very good. My only complaint about this one is that it's either locked shut, or it's popped open about six inches -- those are the only options. You cannot just have it 'resting' closed. If you lock it shut, it gets VERY smelly with dirty dishes after a day. There are just two of us in the house, so we do not run it every day. I want to close it but not lock it -- having the door open six inches is very disruptive to the flow in the kitchen.

Sentence (English): Our old dishwasher died recently, so we had to replace it.
Comments (English): [ Replacement dishwasher ] || ---------------- || Our old dishwasher died recently, so we had to replace it. My wife shopped around and we settled on a new Bosch. We have had it for over a month now. On the plus side, it does get the dishes clean. I have not had any technical issues with it. I like the projected red light (onto the floor) so you can monitor it from across the room. I also like the WiFi synch up so that my phone tells me when a cycle is complete. That said, I still prefer my older dishwasher. The 2 main issues I have with this one are that it takes more than twice as long to run a cycle (2 hours and 10 minutes, minimum) and that it seems to hold less dishes per cycle. There are a huge number of configurations you can set (to maximize # of dishes) but none seem that efficient. I liked the older config better, where it was standard every time so you could learn how to utilize the one setting, as opposed to figuring out how to reconfigure the dishwasher. It's a lot like modern car audio systems - all screens, no knobs, and much less useful than older models. Unfortunately you cannot opt to just have non-configurable racks (that I know of) so you have to make do. None of this has been a huge issue so far, but on those rare occasions when there are 3 or more loads of dishes to do, this will become a multi-day affair. In all fairness, I have heard that newer models across the board take longer to run cycles (due to energy efficiency requirements or some such), so that factor is not specific to Bosch. However, if I'm going to spend this much on a brand new appliance, I'd hope to like it better or get some advantage out of it versus the one that came before. I just don't get that vibe now.

I like the projected red light (onto the floor) so you can monitor it from across the room. I also like the WiFi synch up so that my phone tells me when a cycle is complete. That said, I still prefer my older dishwasher. The 2 main issues I have with this one are that it takes more than twice as long to run a cycle (2 hours and 10 minutes, minimum) and that it seems to hold less dishes per cycle. There are a huge number of configurations you can set (to maximize # of dishes) but none seem that efficient. I liked the older config better, where it was standard every time so you could learn how to utilize the one setting, as opposed to figuring out how to reconfigure the dishwasher. It's a lot like modern car audio systems - all screens, no knobs, and much less useful than older models. Unfortunately you cannot opt to just have non-configurable racks (that I know of) so you have to make do. None of this has been a huge issue so far, but on those rare occasions when there are 3 or more loads of dishes to do, this will become a multi-day affair. In all fairness, I have heard that newer models across the board take longer to run cycles (due to energy efficiency requirements or some such), so that factor is not specific to Bosch. However, if I'm going to spend this much on a brand new appliance, I'd hope to like it better or get some advantage out of it versus the one that came before. I just don't get that vibe now.

Sentence (English): We're delighted with this LG dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Save time and take care of your dishes ] || ---------------- || We're delighted with this LG dishwasher. It has a large capacity thanks to its three racks and multiple adjustment options (cutlery tray, height-adjustable tray, and adjustable shelves). It has a multitude of programs and settings, and the most convenient thing is that you can control it and view the program status on your phone with the ThinQ app. Another positive aspect is how quiet it is during wash cycles compared to other dishwashers we've had in the past, and it's a Class C in energy consumption. I've tried putting in dishes with different types of sauces and stuck-on food residue to test its washing power, and surprisingly, it handled everything, even tomato stains on plastic containers, which are always tedious to remove. Regarding drying, previously there was almost always some water left on cups or cutlery, but with this one everything comes out completely dry. In short, if you're looking for a quiet, large-capacity, modular, powerful dishwasher with remote control, look no further; this one exceeds all expectations.

Men don’t know how hard it is to wash heavy pots and plates every day. I bought it because I absolutely had to get it in. When people gather in our big house, my mom cooks and washes the dishes by herself, and there are limits to how much we can help her, and it’s also very hygienic to occasionally sterilize at high temperatures with the dishwasher, so I bought a 3-stage one. I sometimes turn the hood cover, and when the amount is small, I put it in the sink basin and turn it one layer. This is actually something she used when we came and did by hand, but it’s really good when the whole family gathers. This model uses salt to soften the lime in tap water, but honestly, it doesn’t matter if you don’t put it in. It just removes water stains, but some places give you a free rinse when you buy detergent, and you can just skip it because you don't use the rinse. One of the reasons I chose this model was because it had a three-drawer design. When I used a small one, the spoons would overlap each other, so there were one or two that I didn't wash. But when I spread it out and washed it, it washed really cleanly. I'm completely satisfied. When washing plastic, avoid high temperatures as much as possible, and if you put detergent in the hole in the detergent box? and press the run button, the detergent will come out, but you can just throw it inside. When you put detergent in this box, sometimes the plastic gets caught and the detergent doesn't come out cleanly, and some parts remain, so I just break one or half and throw it on the floor, or when washing baby bottles, I buy a type 1 detergent and spray it on the floor. My mom said that her son doesn't know a woman's heart, and she's so happy that you're here. The driver was also very kind. Thank you.

So, I looked for a device that 1) could be used all year round, 2) could wash baby bottles and baby food, and 3) offered a variety of features like hot air drying and a door opening. Also, I think an automatic door-opening function is essential for a dishwasher, and it's unmatched in this price range for its capacity. I also used the bottle tray I purchased with it, and it worked flawlessly. (Regarding after-sales service, I actually had a problem with the product I received. After only using it once or twice, an error code popped up, making it unusable. I contacted customer service with the error code, and they replaced it right away. It's been a month now, and I'm extremely satisfied with my Minix dishwasher.

I'd been worrying about structural modifications and installation issues, which had kept me from putting it in, but my worries were unnecessary. Comments (Original): [ 식세기 이모님이 일을 잘 하십니다. ] || ---------------- || 설걷이 노동에서 벗어나 기쁩니다.  그동안 싱크대 구조변경 및 설치 문제로 고민만 하다가 들여 놓지 못 했는데, 괜한 걱정이었습니다.  구조변경 없이 가스렌지 아래 싱크장에 정확히 딱 맞아서 쉽고 간단하게 기사님이 설치해 주셨으며, 몰딩 절단비 3만원만 들었습니다.  제품 성능 및 조작, 결과물은 두말할 나위 없고, 여러 기능 필요없고, 식세기 전용 세제 넣으면 알아서 건조까지 일사천리로 해줍니다.  더 놀라운건 작동되면서 거의 소음을 느끼지 못 할 정도로 조용합니다.  고민의 시간은 불필요한듯 합니다.  저녁 시간이 한가롭고 편해 집니다.  앞치마가 젖을 일도 줄고요...이상 장점입니다. 단점은 조금 더 써봐야 알 듯 합니다.

Sentence (English): This is regarding dishwasher KDTM405PPS, which is essentially Costco's version of the more ubiquitious KDTM404KPS, but cheaper, lighter in weight, and Energy star certified since it was made in 2023 instead of 2020 (and has 2-year warranty from Costco included).
Comments (English): [ Works very well, good layout, and quiet! ] || ---------------- || This is regarding dishwasher KDTM405PPS, which is essentially Costco's version of the more ubiquitious KDTM404KPS, but cheaper, lighter in weight, and Energy star certified since it was made in 2023 instead of 2020 (and has 2-year warranty from Costco included). We've only had it a week, but the in 3 washes we've done so far the dishes have come out very clean, better than our old (~2002) KitchenAid (before it gave up). Even our daily used microwaveable oatmeal bowls where the white interior was slightly brown after years in our old KitchenAid is now whiter again. I a lot of time looking at websites and reviews and going to BestBuy/Home Depot with one example of all our plates/bowls/cups to make sure they all fit since our old one didn't have a 3rd rack. I picked this one because the layout worked best for us of all the brands, fitting 12 big hexagonal plates and cereal/soup bowls in the bottom; small plates, plastic boxes and mugs in the middle rack; and lids and sharp knives, spatulas and egg whisk on the top. Also the deep "V" on the top rack works really great for our North glasses (which have big indents in the bottom in the shape of various mountains) which collect water when upright/slightly tilted in the middle rack; on the top rack they're more like 45 degrees and don't collect water so they're dry when you take them out. I was torn between this model and the $150 cheaper KDTE204KPS (with thinner 3rd rack, and triple filtration instead of self-cleaning) because the KDTE model is quieter at only 39bDA vs 44dBA, but the 44dBA one is already so quiet you can hardly tell it's running if not for the light indicator on the front. So I'm glad I went with KDTM, primarily for the bigger upper rack holding North glasses.My only minor quibbles are 1) is I don't like the "type 3" cutlery rack because it had different sized holes so you have to faff about finding the right one for your spoon vs teaspoon vs fork and NONE of them fit our regular dinner knives - luckily I'd read someone's review about this so kept the rack from our old one and use that instead. 2) the spacing of the tines on the middle rack is not as good as the old model -they are wider so don't hold as many small plates or cups and smaller items can fall through (there's not a lot of space in 3rd rack for all the small items) 3) We only have 2 stemware holders and usually use 4 glasses if we open a bottle of wine. 4) The instruction manual could do with improving, it's mostly about the installation and not much about how to actually use it (especially the time delay, which has the choice of 2h, 4h and 8h instead of only 4h on our older model, allowing us to run it in off-peak hours even if you finish dinner before 8pm)

Comments (English): The inside of the 'stainless steel' door had multiple rust spots on it. The operation instructions were very confusing. The app offered to control the washer from your phone does not work well. Loading the trays is difficult because of the direction of the holders sticking up on angles. A lot of wasted space because of that. After the wash is complete and an ample drying time, there is still a lot of water/condensation on the inside of the door and top of the washer that drip onto the clean dry dishes. On a positive note it is VERY quiet. As for delivery, I paid to have it delivered and installed and the old one removed. When it was delivered they informed me that they did not install nor remove the old one. They told me I would need to hire a contractor. A big disappointment. I did get my money back quickly after a call to HD customer service.

Comments (English): [ A proper dishwasher ] || ---------------- || I recently upgraded to this Bosch dishwasher, replacing my old builder-grade 5-year-old GE Café model. I had a Bosch in my previous home and really missed the speed, capacity, and quiet operation it offers.The installation process was handled by Elite Installation (based in Raleigh, NC), and it was flawless. It's a handy feature that adds extra convenience to an already fantastic product.Another highlight is the CrystalDry feature. My glassware comes out looking sparkling clean every time. The CrystalDry mode completes in 2hrs:45mins, CrystalDry with Sanitize completes in 3:h 03mins. When the price dropped by $100 within 14 days of my purchase, I made a quick call to their automated system. The process was smooth, and I received the refund within 48 hours.Overall, I couldn't be happier with this dishwasher and the entire experience, from installation to performance and customer service. Highly recommended!

Sentence (English): Recently, my Kitchenaid dishwasher broke and I replaced it with a Bosch 300 Series.
Comments (English): [ Delivery and Installation experience ] || ---------------- || Recently, my Kitchenaid dishwasher broke and I replaced it with a Bosch 300 Series. I am a fan of Costco because of their high customer satisfaction and have had mostly positive experiences on big ticket items (appliance, trip, shed and etc). Therefore, I was surprised to see many negative reviews about the delivery process and/or damaged product and was a bit worry and hesitant making this purchase. I took the risk based on my past experiences and I was not disappointed. I don't usually write reviews and I wanted to take some time to do this because I had a seamless and great experience ordering my dishwasher from Costco. MasterPro (Costco's installation vendor) contacted me shortly after I placed my order and they were very good with their communication and time frame on my delivery. I did read their instructions about making sure the require clearance of 34" and an air gap are there for the installers to properly do the hookup. Sentence (English): I think we got a lemon.
Comments (English): [ We thinks it's a "lemon". ] || ---------------- || I think we got a lemon. We had to wait a month for delivery because it was on backorder. When it finally arrived and we were able to install it, we discovered it was filled with water. Not just wet inside, but probably at least a gallon of water poured out into the kitchen from the water outlet. It's been installed for less than 1 month. There are only two adults that make up our household. I put the rinse aid in and used the detergent tabs it came with. The first wash came out OK. A few dishes still had some dried food particles on them. I felt a little worried, but still gave it the benefit of the doubt. I thought maybe I didn't pick the right cycle. I told myself to read the user manual online. The second time I used it, the soap dispenser had not opened, so I had to run it again. The third time the dishes were still a bit dirty and I started to think we made a mistake with this dishwasher. The fourth time, we don't know what happened because I hit start and left for work and when I came home, eight hours later, it was still running with the same amount of runtime still left on the timer and nothing had progressed with the wash. I turned it off and started it again and this time, it ran through the cycle properly, but the dishes were still dirty. Some even dirtier than they went in. I don't know what to do now because I know Home Depot isn't going to help me since it's been a month since they delivered it. Does GE send a repair person out? Will they know what needs to be repaired considering the plethora of issues? Do they stay for three hours while it runs to make sure the dishes come out clean/soap dispenser has opened or check that it doesn't run for eight hours and does nothing? We do have hard water, but I use the rinse aid and a quality detergent. I do not put the dishes in without rinsing them. Either I rinse them in the sink or my dog does a quality pre-rinse job before they go in. (If you are a dog owner, You get it if you're not, you probably think I'm a weirdo.) My coffee cups come out with coffee stains dried in them or specks of food that were not in them in the first place. Plates have dried food particles.Other than the fact that it doesn't clean, and several different aspects of malfunction, it's very quiet and I like the third rack for spatulas and other utensils.

Comments (English): [ Convenience of life ] || ---------------- || A guy who was better at washing dishes than me came to my house. I didn't buy it because I thought I'd just do the dishes. I don't know what to do now because I know Home Depot isn't going to help me since it's been a month since they delivered it. Does GE send a repair person out? Will they know what needs to be repaired considering the plethora of issues? Do they stay for three hours while it runs to make sure the dishes come out clean/soap dispenser has opened or check that it doesn't run for eight hours and does nothing? We do have hard water, but I use the rinse aid and a quality detergent. I do not put the dishes in without rinsing them. Either I rinse them in the sink or my dog does a quality pre-rinse job before they go in. (If you are a dog owner, You get it if you're not, you probably think I'm a weirdo.) My coffee cups come out with coffee stains dried in them or specks of food that were not in them in the first place. Plates have dried food particles. Other than the fact that it doesn't clean, and several different aspects of malfunction, it's very quiet and I like the third rack for spatulas and other utensils.

Sentence (English): I've only had the dishwasher for a week or two, but the difference in the dishes is noticeable.
Comments (English): [ Quiet and Competent ] || ---------------- || I've only had the dishwasher for a week or two, but the difference in the dishes is noticeable. Granted, I was coming from a 20 year old Kenmore, but even counting the dishwashers I've had the pleasure or displeasure of experiencing before (GE, Kitchenaid, Samsung) this dishwasher is as quiet and thorough as dishwashers hundreds more in price. It dries well, too, if you put the heated dry on. I'm thoroughly enjoying the third rack for the silverware and cup lids, but the dish rack down below has a cover for the silverware areas if needed, as well. I will admit that it's taking some time to get used to the taller tines on the bottom rack and how to fit things in (I could really cram that Kenmore, I'll admit), but I don't think it warrants losing a star over. So far, so good! I chose this one for the price and the recommendation from Consumer Reports and am happy I did!

Sentence (English): I owned the Bosch 300 model before this one and I am sad to report that on this iteration Bosch have "cheaped out.
Comments (English): [ Not bad but not as good ] || ---------------- || I owned the Bosch 300 model before this one and I am sad to report that on this iteration Bosch have "cheaped out."While it is still a reasonable dishwasher it also has to be remembered that it is getting towards the "premium" price range and the cost cutting in the manufacturing rankles.So where did Bosch cut costs? They shrunk the cutlery holder by at least half. Fortunately for me I hadn't disposed of the old one, so for me it was an easy swap.They have also reduced the amount of sound insulation material. This results in a noisier machine when it washes. The previous Bosch 300 I could barely hear while it was in operation and occasionally it surprised me when I actually heard it working. This one is much noisier and I can hear it from another room. It is not the loudest dishwasher I have heard but substantially louder than its predecessor. By removing some of that insulation I would imagine that it is slightly more expensive to use because heat will leak more rapidly causing the heater to work a little harder.The previous Bosch 300 was a joy to use but sadly this one is a bit of a pain. On the old model all of the functions could be utilised from the front panel including setting up a delayed start. Sadly Bosch have decided that an app is what we all need. In these days of 5,000 apps on our phones for everything and decreasing privacy another app is what we all want isn't it? Especially when it seems to be shared with Siemens.Unfortunately the app is the only way to access some dishwasher functions s uch as delayed start so aside from being stuck with itmost will find it difficult to use with next to no guidance.After 8 days I still feel as though I need to "join hands and make contact with the living" for its operation. Let's be straight; I may be 65 but I have been using computers since 1981and if I'm having problems. Does this dishwasher wash dishes etc? Yes! Is it good at it? Yes! So not all is lost but remember it is not up to the high standards that Bosch set for themselves.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher is slightly better than some others currently on the market, which isn't saying much.
Comments (English): [ Worst Detergent Container Ever ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher is slightly better than some others currently on the market, which isn't saying much. Unlike some others which unaccountably are built today with no heating element and leave dishes soaking wet, this one mostly dries the dishes and leaves the interior of the dishwasher only lightly damp. Why damp at all? Who knows. My old dishwasher - only about 9 years old before its electrical control panel went out and we found they no longer make that control panel anywhere - never left dishes wet and was never coated with dampness at the end of a run. The WORST thing about this dishwasher is the terrible cup that is meant to hold detergent. Unlike solid old-style detergent cups that closed securely whether you used powder, liquid or those terrible micro-plastic residue "pods", this one will NOT snap shut if you are even a tiny bit off in the amount of detergent you pour in. It is TERRIBLE, and worst of all is the new "style" for all new dishwashers on the market. WHY would they make a change that makes using the appliance difficult in a way that was never difficult in the past 30 years of dishwasher design? We currently have a bit too much powder that spilled into the cup area, and no matter how much we scoop out, the cup will not close. We have been trying for 10 minutes and getting detergent everywhere, but we're still stuck and unable to close the flimsy little stupid flap so we can start the appliance for the night. "Troubleshooting" on the website gives us no solution.THIS MUST BE CHANGED BACK TO THE GOOD, SOLID FORMER DESIGN. I find this nothing better than a design defect.

Grrrr.

Sentence (English): We had our previous Bosch dishwasher for 20+ years.
Comments (English): [ A great dishwasher, but… ] || ---------------- || We had our previous Bosch dishwasher for 20+ years. Our new 800 series is an amazing improvement over our last dishwasher. Note that we are giving the dishwasher five stars, but there are a couple things about the 800 series that we wish it had. First, it would be nice to have some way to tell you the dishwasher has run and is finished. Our old dishwasher had a couple lights on the control panel that told you it was done. This model has nothing to tell you it's done. We've solved this by putting a small, humorous statue on top of the counter above the dishwasher. Second, no matter how many times we've watched the Bosch videos on how to load the dishwasher, we have yet to find our perfect load strategy. Maybe after a few more months. To close on a positive note, we love that the dishwasher only uses about 2.6 gallons of water per Economy load.

Sentence (English): I want to share my horrendously negative experience so it will hopefully save someone else from a similar experience.
Comments (English): [ Worst experience ever ] || ---------------- || I want to share my horrendously negative experience so it will hopefully save someone else from a similar experience. The review is mostly about my experience with GE (which is who you would be dealing with if you have issues) but I bought it from Lowe's so I thought it may be helpful for others looking for a dishwasher at Lowe's. I bought this dishwasher from Lowe's in April of 2024. It almost immediately started leaking moisture. Steam escaped and pooled under my countertops until it dripped on the floor. After 3-4 service calls by GE, the unit was finally deemed unrepairable and they replaced it with another unit. The second unit is having the same exact issues. After another 3 service calls, I was told the unit is still repairable. They want to send another technician out to confirm it's actually not repairable. They said they might be able to offer me another replacement for a different unit at that point. I also found out that GE knew this model was having this issue (an internal service bulletin was issued for this model/serial number) yet they replaced the unit with the same model. GE is selling and providing units which they know are leaking moisture. The “best case” outcome right now is I get another GE dishwasher which I do not want since I have lost all trust and respect for GE. Each service call required me to stay home from work and wait hours for the technician. I have spent so much time, money, and energy on this dishwasher. I wish so badly I never purchased it. I am buying a dishwasher from a different company, because spending another $1000 is a million times less painful than spending any more time with this GE. You may have better luck, but I would strongly advise to please please please stay away.
